previous_disclosures.summary: Fiscal year 2023 gross margin declined due to $2.17 billion in inventory charges related to excess supply of NVIDIA Ampere architecture Gaming and Data Center products versus demand expectations, particularly in China. These charges comprised $1.04 billion for inventory on hand and $1.13 billion for inventory purchase obligations.

previous_disclosures.summary: Gross margin was 56.9% for fiscal year 2023, a decrease from 64.9% in fiscal year 2022, primarily due to $2.17 billion in inventory provisions.

current_disclosures.summary: Gross margin increased in fiscal year 2024, primarily driven by Data Center revenue growth and lower net inventory provisions as a percentage of revenue.

current_disclosures.section: Results of Operations > Gross Profit and Gross Margin
current_disclosures.summary: Overall gross margin increased to 72.7% in fiscal year 2024 from 56.9% in fiscal year 2023, primarily driven by 217% Data Center revenue growth and lower net inventory provisions as a percentage of revenue.

materiality_analysis.reason: Gross margin improved drastically from 56.9% to 72.7%, driven by the elimination of the $2.17 billion inventory charge seen in the prior year and massive Data Center growth. This represents a fundamental improvement in profitability and operational efficiency.
materiality_analysis.key_change: Significant increase in gross margin due to removal of inventory provisions

target_year_over_year_context.explanation: Both disclosures address the increase in gross margin for their respective fiscal years, attributing the primary driver to Data Center revenue growth/mix.

previous_disclosures.summary: Gross margin increased in fiscal year 2024, primarily driven by Data Center revenue growth and lower net inventory provisions as a percentage of revenue.

current_disclosures.summary: Gross margin increased in fiscal year 2025 due to a higher mix of Data Center revenue.

materiality_analysis.reason: The disclosure updates the explanation for gross margin increases from 'Data Center revenue growth and lower net inventory provisions' (FY24) to 'higher mix of Data Center revenue' (FY25). This is a standard analytical update reflecting the dominant cost structure drivers in a high-growth technology company. It does not indicate a change in cost structure, pricing power, or operational efficiency that constitutes a material new risk or condition, but rather the financial result of the business strategy.
materiality_analysis.key_change: Refinement of gross margin driver attribution

comparisons.peer_summary: Gross margin as a percentage of net revenue increased to 49% in 2024 from 46% in 2023. This increase was primarily driven by a favorable shift in revenue mix towards higher Data Center and Client revenues, as well as lower Gaming revenue, which was partially offset by the impact of lower Embedded revenue.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD report an increase in gross margin for fiscal year 2024 driven by shifts in product mix and growth in the Data Center segment. NVDA attributes its margin increase to 'Data Center revenue growth and lower net inventory provisions,' while AMD cites a 'favorable shift in revenue mix of higher Data Center and Client revenues' as the primary driver. However, the magnitude and composition differ: NVDA's gross margin rose significantly with emphasis on inventory provision benefits, whereas AMD's margin increased from 46% to 49% primarily due to revenue mix, though AMD also noted that lower Gaming revenue was a factor, unlike NVDA's focus on inventory provisions.

sentences.text: Gross margin increased in fiscal year 2024, primarily driven by Data Center revenue growth and lower net inventory provisions as a percentage of revenue.
Gross margin as a percentage of net revenue was 49% in 2024 compared to 46% in 2023.
The increase in gross margin was due to a favorable shift in revenue mix of higher Data Center and Client revenues, lower Gaming revenue, partially offset by the impact of lower Embedded revenue.
